reasoning:
Hard gate fails: kelvin_ok=false (kelvin_unrouted=1), gates_pass=false. Cable 1 has a symmetric Kelvin failure (both /SENSEC1_HI and /SENSEC1_LO unrouted) → Rule 33 fires. Cable 2 has an asymmetric failure (/SENSEC2_HI unrouted, /SENSEC2_LO routed) → Rule 50 fires. Since both fire on different cable indices in the same round, Rule 51 fires: round 97 must inject ONLY cable-1 Kelvin stubs with mandatory_kelvin_bypass semantics, suppressing the cable-2 Rule-50 stub and ALL compiler stubs (per Rule 34). Simultaneously, Rule 46 fires: inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected = 7 - 3 = 4 ≥ 1; total stub elimination absorbed+trimmed_spurs+removed_orphans = 3+2+2 = 7 = n_stubs > 0; kelvin_unrouted > 0; compiler nets non-empty ([/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA]). Rule 46 therefore arms absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed=True for round 97, intending to pass CAN_H/I2C stubs through the absorber without elimination.

CRITICAL NEW INTERACTION — Rule 46 bypass nullified by Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass: Rule 46 arms its bypass for round R+1 (round 97). But Rule 51 mandates mandatory_kelvin_bypass for round 97, which per Rule 34 SUPPRESSES ALL COMPILER STUBS in round 97. No compiler stubs for CAN_H/I2C_SCL/I2C_SDA are generated in round 97 because mandatory_kelvin_bypass eliminates them at the compiler output stage — the absorber bypass has nothing to operate on. Rule 46 then resets absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed=False immediately after round 97 is dispatched, so the bypass is gone before round 98 where compiler stubs could again appear. The net_absorption_count suppression for round 96 (the other half of Rule 46) still correctly fires, but the absorber-bypass half — the mechanism that allows CAN_H/I2C stubs to survive to FR in at least one round — is silently nullified. These nets may therefore continue accumulating false-positive absorptions toward the Rule 49 deadlock-exclusion threshold without ever receiving the bypass round that would confirm whether FR can complete them. This interaction is not covered by any of Rules 46, 49, 51, or 34 individually.

DRC=36 remains high (structural violations at shunt-cluster region likely contributing to Kelvin path blockage). diffpair_ok=true is the only positive gate.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Raising drc penalty from 140→175 increases selection pressure against structurally congested routes. DRC=36 is persistently co-elevated with Kelvin failures across many rounds, indicating geometric conflict near shunt clusters is both a DRC problem and a Kelvin routing problem. A stronger DRC penalty (delta ~1260 in objective space at DRC=36) incentivises FR toward structurally cleaner solutions that open escape paths for Kelvin pairs, without approaching the magnitude of gate_fail/kelvin_unrouted penalties (which must remain primary). The 35-point raise is deliberately incremental: enough to meaningfully shift candidate ranking under high-DRC conditions without distorting objective landscape for normal DRC ranges.

manager_rule: Detect Rule-46 + Rule-51 co-fire and defer the Rule-46 absorber bypass by one round. After each round R: if Rule 46 fires (absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed set to True, with a non-empty compiler nets list) AND Rule 51 also fires in the SAME round R (both Rule 33 for cable C_sym AND Rule 50 for cable C_asym trigger simultaneously): (1) store the round R compiler nets list as a session-scoped set 'deferred_rule46_bypass_nets', e.g. {/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA}; (2) in round R+1, Rule 51's mandatory_kelvin_bypass correctly suppresses all compiler stubs per Rule 34 — do NOT attempt to apply Rule 46's absorber bypass in round R+1 (it has nothing to operate on); (3) in round R+2, if the compiler generates stubs for any net in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets, pass those stubs through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages WITHOUT elimination, treating them as exempt from absorption for round R+2 only (the same bypass-pass-through semantics Rule 46 would have applied in R+1); do NOT suppress net_absorption_count increments in R+2 since the false-positive risk is re-evaluated fresh from R+2's round state; (4) reset deferred_rule46_bypass_nets to empty immediately after round R+2 is dispatched regardless of outcome; (5) log 'rule46_rule51_cofire_bypass_deferral' with fields: (a) round R, (b) C_sym and C_asym from Rule 51, (c) nets in deferred_rule46_bypass_nets, (d) confirmation that bypass is deferred to R+2 because mandatory_kelvin_bypass in R+1 suppresses all compiler stubs, (e) net_absorption_count suppression status for round R (still applied per Rule 46 even when bypass is deferred). This rule is additive to Rules 34, 46, and 51 and does not modify any other session-scoped state or replace any action those rules independently mandate. Rationale: Rule 51 mandates mandatory_kelvin_bypass for round R+1, which per Rule 34 suppresses ALL compiler stubs; Rule 46 arms absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed=True for round R+1 expecting compiler stubs to be present, but those stubs are suppressed before they reach the absorber — the bypass fires on an empty set and then Rule 46 resets the flag before round R+2. The CAN_H/I2C nets that triggered Rule 46 never receive the bypass round that would allow FR to route them under guidance, while their net_absorption_count suppression (correctly applied in R) means they accumulate no false-positive absorptions toward Rule 49's deadlock-exclusion threshold but also receive no routing opportunity. Deferring the bypass by one round preserves Rule 46's intent across the mandatory_kelvin_bypass suppression window.
